reports.title: Ontario Budget
reports.description: Annual provincial budget document presenting the government's economic outlook, fiscal plan, revenue and expense projections, borrowing program, and policy measures. Includes the multi-year path to balance, net debt-to-GDP projections, and detailed fiscal tables. Most recent: 2026 Ontario Budget: A Plan to Protect Ontario (tabled March 2026). Supplemented intra-year by First Quarter Finances and other quarterly updates.
reports.cadence_note: Annual (typically spring); supplemented by Fall Economic Outlook and Fiscal Review and quarterly finances updates

reports.title: Public Accounts of Ontario
reports.publisher: Treasury Board Secretariat / Ontario Ministry of Finance (audited by Auditor General of Ontario)
reports.description: Annual audited consolidated financial statements of the Province of Ontario for the fiscal year ended 31 March, including the Annual Report, Consolidated Financial Statements, Ministry Statements and Schedules, and Detailed Schedules of Payments. Prepared under Canadian public sector accounting standards and compared against the Budget plan.

reports.title: Ontario Financing Authority
reports.publisher: Ontario Financing Authority (agency of the Province of Ontario)
reports.description: Crown agency that conducts borrowing, investment and financial risk management for the Province, manages the provincial debt, and executes the long-term public borrowing program set out in the Ontario Budget. Publishes annual reports, financial statements, borrowing program status, and investor presentations. Directly implements the funding requirements and debt-management strategy of the Budget.
reports.cadence_note: Continuous operational reporting; Annual Report and financial statements yearly

reports.title: Financial Accountability Office of Ontario
reports.publisher: Financial Accountability Office of Ontario (independent officer of the Legislative Assembly)
reports.description: Independent office established by the Financial Accountability Officer Act, 2013. Provides non-partisan analysis to the Legislative Assembly on the state of the Province’s finances (including the Budget), trends in the provincial and national economies, expenditure estimates, and the financial costs/benefits of public bills or proposals. Issues Budget Notes, Economic and Budget Outlook reports, and annual reports.
reports.cadence_note: Multiple reports per year; Annual Report

reports.title: City of Toronto Operating and Capital Budget
reports.description: Annual tax- and rate-supported operating budget and multi-year capital budget and plan adopted by City Council (Mayor's proposed budget under City of Toronto Act). Includes property-tax levy requirements, service-area allocations, and 10-year capital plan. Most recent: 2026 Operating Budget ($18.9 billion) and 2026–2035 Capital Budget and Plan ($63.1 billion).

reports.title: City of Toronto Consolidated Financial Statements / Annual Financial Report
reports.publisher: City of Toronto (Finance & Treasury; audited by external auditor)
reports.description: Audited consolidated financial statements (including sinking funds and trust funds) prepared in accordance with Canadian public sector accounting standards (PSAB). Accompanied by the Annual Financial Report providing narrative and statistical context. Most recent complete: 2024 statements approved 2025; 2025 draft statements available 2026.

reports.title: City of Toronto Tax Levy By-law
reports.description: Annual by-law enacted under the City of Toronto Act setting the municipal tax ratios, general local municipal levy, additional rates for budgetary increase and City Building Fund, and resulting tax rates by property class. Generates the property-tax revenue authorized by the adopted budget. Example: By-law 133-2026 (Tax Levy By-law for 2026).

reports.title: City of Toronto Long-Term Financial Plan
reports.description: Multi-year framework for longer-term financial decision-making, strategies and key actions to support integrated, strategic budgeting. Updated Long-Term Financial Plan adopted September 2023; subsequent status updates appear in annual budget processes and Annual Financial Reports. Provides the roadmap that informs the annual Operating and Capital Budgets.
reports.cadence_note: Periodic major updates (most recent 2023) with annual status reporting

reports.title: City of Ottawa Operating and Capital Budget
reports.description: Annual tax- and rate-supported operating budget and capital budget adopted by Council under the Municipal Act. Must be balanced. Includes property-tax levy, transit levy, water/sewer rates, and multi-year capital authority. Example: 2025 Adopted Budget; 2026 draft presented late 2025.

reports.title: City of Ottawa Consolidated Financial Statements / Annual Report
reports.publisher: City of Ottawa (Finance and Corporate Services; audited by external auditor)
reports.description: Audited consolidated financial statements prepared in accordance with Canadian public sector accounting standards (PSAB) as required by the Municipal Act, accompanied by the Annual Report containing financial statement discussion and analysis and statistical schedules. Most recent: 2024 Annual Report (released 2025); 2025 statements presented 2026.

reports.title: City of Ottawa Tax Policy and Annual Tax Rate Bylaws
reports.description: Council-approved tax ratios by property class and subclass, together with the annual bylaws that establish municipal tax rates based on the adopted budget levy requirement and MPAC assessment. Equivalent function to Toronto’s Tax Levy By-law. Includes small-business subclass, multi-residential ratio path, and capping/clawback parameters.
reports.cadence_note: Annual (ratios and rates set each year)

reports.title: Ontario Education Tax Rates (O. Reg. 400/98 as amended)
reports.publisher: Ontario Ministry of Finance (Minister of Finance)
reports.description: Annual regulation under the Education Act prescribing the tax rates for school purposes that every municipality must levy and collect on rateable property. Rates are set by the Minister of Finance (most recent update O. Reg. 297/25 for 2026). Municipalities apply these rates to MPAC assessments alongside their own municipal rates. Education portion typically ~20-25% of a residential tax bill.

reports.title: City of Toronto Municipal Land Transfer Tax (MLTT) and Municipal Non-Resident Speculation Tax
reports.description: Municipal Land Transfer Tax levied on property conveyances in Toronto (Toronto Municipal Code Chapter 760) plus the Municipal Non-Resident Speculation Tax (10% on eligible foreign buyers, effective 2025). Graduated rate structure for high-value residential properties updated 2026. Significant own-source revenue tool referenced in the Long-Term Financial Plan and annual budgets.
reports.cadence_note: Rates and structure updated by bylaw as needed; ongoing administration

reports.title: City of Mississauga Budget
reports.description: Annual operating and capital budget adopted by Council. Includes City portion of property tax levy (Region of Peel and education are separate). Most recent: 2026 Budget adopted January 2026.

reports.title: City of Mississauga Consolidated Financial Statements / Financial and Sustainability Report
reports.description: Audited consolidated financial statements prepared in accordance with Public Sector Accounting Board standards as required by the Municipal Act, 2001, accompanied by the Financial and Sustainability Report.

reports.title: City of Mississauga Tax Ratios and Rates By-law
reports.description: Annual by-law establishing tax ratios and levies for the year (e.g. By-law 0061-2026). Property tax calculated as MPAC assessment × combined City + Region of Peel + education rates.

reports.title: City of Hamilton Tax & Rate Budget
reports.description: Annual tax-supported operating and capital budget plus rate-supported (water) budget. Adopted under Municipal Act / Strong Mayor powers. Includes Property Tax Levy By-law.

reports.title: City of Hamilton Consolidated Financial Statements
reports.description: Audited consolidated financial statements and statistical information prepared under Canadian public sector accounting standards.

reports.title: City of Brampton Budget
reports.description: Annual operating and capital budget. City portion of property tax; Region of Peel and education collected on behalf of others. 2026 Budget featured 0% increase on City portion.

reports.title: City of Brampton Consolidated Financial Statements / Financial Report
reports.description: Audited consolidated financial statements prepared under Canadian public sector accounting standards / PSAB, published in the annual Financial Report.

reports.title: City of London Multi-Year Budget
reports.description: Multi-year (currently 2024–2027) property-tax and rate-supported budget with annual updates. Sets the tax levy requirement used to calculate rates.

reports.title: City of London Consolidated Financial Statements / Financial Report
reports.description: Audited consolidated financial statements prepared under Public Sector Accounting Standards, published in the annual Financial Report.

reports.title: City of London Tax Rates and Codes
reports.description: Annual tax rates and codes set by Council after budget adoption. Calculated from the tax levy requirement and MPAC assessments; education rates applied as prescribed by the Province.

reports.title: City of Guelph Multi-Year Budget / Confirmed Budget
reports.description: Multi-year budget (e.g. 2024–2027) with annual confirmed updates. Sets the City tax levy requirement used for rate calculation. Includes local boards and shared services and hospital levy components.

reports.title: City of Guelph Consolidated Financial Statements
reports.description: Audited consolidated financial statements prepared under Canadian public sector accounting standards / Municipal Act requirements. Clean (unqualified) audit opinions routinely received.

reports.title: City of Guelph Property Tax Rates
reports.description: Published annual tax rates by property class combining City levy, hospital levy (where applicable), and provincial education rates applied to MPAC assessment.

reports.title: City of Kingston Operating and Capital Budgets
reports.description: Annual operating and capital budgets proposed under Strong Mayor powers and adopted by Council. Includes tax levy requirement.

reports.title: City of Kingston Consolidated Financial Statements
reports.description: Audited consolidated financial statements prepared under Canadian public sector accounting standards.

reports.title: City of Kingston Tax Levy By-law
reports.description: Annual by-law setting and levying tax rates based on the adopted budget and the returned assessment roll. Includes schedules for municipal general, area rates, and education.

reports.title: Town of Caledon Budget
reports.description: Annual operating and capital budget. Includes property tax increase plus dedicated infrastructure levy. Lower-tier municipality within Region of Peel.

reports.title: Town of Caledon Consolidated Financial Statements
reports.description: Audited consolidated financial statements prepared under Canadian public sector accounting standards as required by the Municipal Act.

reports.title: Town of Caledon Tax Rates / Levy
reports.description: Annual tax rates set by Council after budget adoption. Combined with Region of Peel and education rates on MPAC assessment. Includes infrastructure levy component.

reports.title: Town of Cobourg Tax Rates
reports.description: Published tax rates and illustrative bill breakdown showing Town, County, and education portions calculated on MPAC current-value assessment.

reports.title: The Canadian Consumer Price Index Reference Paper
reports.description: Authoritative methodology document explaining the conceptual, structural and methodological basis of the Canadian CPI: scope, classifications, sample strategy, price collection, index calculation, quality adjustment, basket weights and updates, reliability, and history. Updated periodically (2023 edition is the current comprehensive reference).

reports.title: City of Toronto Councillor / Mayor Remuneration – CPI Adjustment
reports.description: During the term of Council, remuneration paid to the Mayor and Councillors is adjusted annually to the Statistics Canada Consumer Price Index (CPI) for Toronto, as calculated by the Deputy City Manager and Chief Financial Officer based on the previous year’s average (Council policy originating 2006, with subsequent reviews).

reports.title: Public Service Pension Plan (PSPP) Cost-of-Living Adjustment (COLA) Methodology
reports.description: Formal formula for annual COLA applied to PSPP pensions in pay. Escalation factor is calculated from the average Statistics Canada Consumer Price Index over two consecutive 12-month periods ending 30 September. Maximum annual increase 8%; excess carried forward. Applied each January. Primary provincial mechanism that directly indexes a major compensation stream to CPI.

reports.title: MPP Pension and Compensation Act, 2025
reports.publisher: Legislative Assembly of Ontario / Government of Ontario
reports.description: Legislation that ended the multi-year MPP salary freeze. Sets base MPP salary at 75% of the federal Member of Parliament sessional allowance (effective with the 2025 election), with subsequent annual increases tied to federal MP salaries. Also establishes a new pension arrangement integrated with the Public Service Pension Plan plus a supplemental benefit for members with at least six years of service (effective 1 January 2026).
reports.cadence_note: One-time statute; annual salary adjustments thereafter

reports.title: Ontario Works Policy Directives
reports.publisher: Ministry of Children, Community and Social Services / Government of Ontario
reports.description: Official policy directives for the Ontario Works program covering eligibility, calculation of assistance, basic needs, shelter, and related benefits. Rates are set by regulation; unlike ODSP they are not currently on an automatic inflation index.
reports.cadence_note: Standing directives; rates updated by regulation

reports.title: Ontario Guaranteed Annual Income System (GAINS) Benefit Rates
reports.publisher: Ministry of Finance / Government of Ontario
reports.description: Official rate tables for the Guaranteed Annual Income System, a provincial top-up for low-income seniors receiving federal Old Age Security and Guaranteed Income Supplement. Tables published by age band (65–74 and 75+) and private income level; updated periodically (often quarterly).

reports.title: City of Toronto Property Tax & Utility Relief Programs for Low-Income Seniors and Persons with Disabilities
reports.description: Municipal programs providing property tax increase cancellation or deferral, water rebate, and solid waste relief for eligible low-income seniors and low-income persons with disabilities. Income thresholds and eligibility criteria set by the City; often linked to receipt of GIS or ODSP.

reports.title: City of Mississauga Property Tax Rebate for Low-Income Seniors and Persons with Disabilities
reports.description: Annual property tax rebate program for eligible low-income seniors (65+) and persons with disabilities who own and occupy their home and receive GIS or ODSP. Rate and eligibility set by municipal by-law / program rules.

reports.title: Financial Information Return (FIR) Instructions and Introduction
reports.publisher: Ontario Ministry of Municipal Affairs and Housing
reports.description: The official annual instruction set and introduction for completing the Ontario Financial Information Return. Explicitly states that FIR data must reflect the municipality’s audited financial statements prepared under PSAB standards, details every schedule (taxation, operations, debt, development charges, etc.), and announces the 2027 template rewrite to implement the new PS 1202 reporting model.

reports.title: Ontario School Board Audited Financial Statements and EFIS Reporting
reports.publisher: Ontario Ministry of Education (Financial Analysis & Accountability Branch) / individual district school boards
reports.description: The mandatory annual audited financial statements that every district school board and school authority must prepare under the Education Act (s. 252), submit through the Education Finance Information System (EFIS), and publish on their websites. Prepared in accordance with Canadian Public Sector Accounting Standards. Includes consolidated statements of financial position, operations, cash flow, change in net debt and remeasurement gains/losses.

reports.title: Postsecondary Operating Grants and Strategic Mandate Agreements
reports.publisher: Ontario Ministry of Colleges, Universities, Research Excellence and Security
reports.description: The ministry’s multi-year operating funding to Ontario’s 24 publicly assisted colleges, 23 universities and Indigenous Institutes. Delivered primarily through five-year Strategic Mandate Agreements (SMAs) that link a growing share of funding to performance metrics. Includes the new long-term funding model announced in 2026 that raises annual operating funding toward $7 billion and adds STEM and sustainability envelopes.

reports.title: Ontario Tuition Framework for Publicly Assisted Colleges and Universities
reports.publisher: Ontario Ministry of Colleges, Universities, Research Excellence and Security
reports.description: The provincial policy that sets the maximum annual tuition increase for domestic students at publicly assisted colleges and universities (currently capped, with a multi-year path allowing up to 2 % then inflation-linked increases). Forms part of the overall revenue framework that complements operating grants.

reports.title: Loyalist Township Municipal Budget (Operating and Capital)
reports.description: The annual operating and capital budget for Loyalist Township (lower-tier municipality in the County of Lennox and Addington). Sets the municipal tax levy requirement (e.g. $24.457 million for 2026) that is subsequently translated into tax rates via the annual tax-rate by-law. Publicly deliberated and finalized by Council.

reports.title: Loyalist Township Tax Rate By-law
reports.description: The annual by-law (e.g. By-law 2026-19) that establishes tax rates for general and special purposes after adoption of the municipal budget estimates. Explicitly multiplies the latest revised assessment roll (MPAC) by the adopted rates, incorporates County and education rates, and authorizes collection. Required under Municipal Act s. 312.

reports.title: Loyalist Township Audited Financial Statements
reports.description: The annual audited consolidated financial statements prepared under Canadian Public Sector Accounting Standards and submitted as the basis for the municipality's Financial Information Return to the Ministry of Municipal Affairs and Housing.

The document states: "For further information on the concepts and use of the CPI, see The Canadian Consumer Price Index Reference Paper (Catalogue number 62-553-X)."

While the Budget cites the published CPI series, the underlying methodology that defines what the series measures is the Reference Paper; the Budget relies on the official definition of CPI inflation. The document states: "Sources: Statistics Canada and Ontario Ministry of Finance."

Councillor and Mayor remuneration is adjusted annually to the Statistics Canada CPI for Toronto based on the previous year’s average. The document states: "During the term of Council, remuneration paid to the Mayor and Councillors is adjusted annually to the Statistics Canada Consumer Price Index (CPI) for Toronto, as calculated by the Deputy City Manager and Chief Financial Officer and based on the previous year’s average (City Council 2006)."

PSPP COLA escalation factor is calculated directly from Statistics Canada Consumer Price Index averages over defined 12-month periods ending 30 September. The document states: "COLA is calculated using a three-step process: 1. We look at the consumer price index (CPI) over a 24-month period ending September 30 of the current year... 2. For each 12-month period... we calculate the average... 3. Then we divide the average of the second 12-month period by the average of the first..."

The CPI series used in the PSPP formula is the official Statistics Canada CPI whose concepts and calculation methods are defined in the Canadian CPI Reference Paper. The document states: "We are required under our PSPP plan text to calculate COLA using a specific formula based on the consumer price index (CPI)... CPI is a measure of inflation determined by the Canadian Government and released by Statistics Canada."

The new MPP pension arrangement is integrated with the Public Service Pension Plan; MPPs therefore become subject to the same PSPP COLA rules once in receipt of pension. MPPs would join the PSPP on the same terms as other members, plus receive an additional supplementary pension benefit."

The cost of the property-tax relief programs is absorbed within the City’s operating budget / tax levy capacity. The document states: "The City offers various programs including the Property Tax Increase Cancellation Program, Property Tax Increase Deferral Program..."

The municipal rebate is funded from the City’s tax-supported budget. The document states: "The City offers property tax rebates for eligible seniors (65 years and older) with low incomes and people with disabilities with low incomes."

The official FIR Introduction states that the information in the Return must reflect the audited financial statements of the municipality prepared under PSAB standards. The document states: "The information included in the Financial Information Return should reflect the audited financial statements of the municipality (PSAB Standards)."

The FIR Instructions and Introduction repeatedly require municipalities to follow the same PSAB Handbook standards used for their audited financial statements (tangible capital assets PS 3150, government reporting entity PS 1300, asset retirement obligations PS 3280, etc.). The document states: "Please follow the same accounting and financial reporting standards contained in the PSA Handbook: PS 3150 Tangible Capital Assets that are utilized to produce the annual financial statements."

Municipalities complete the FIR using the official annual Instructions and Introduction issued by the Ministry; the template itself contains over 1 400 verification checks derived from those instructions. The document states: "To further assist municipalities with completing the FIR, over 1400 data verification checks are built into the template."

School board audited financial statements are required to be prepared in accordance with Canadian Public Sector Accounting Standards. Auditor General reviews and Ministry illustrative notes confirm this basis of accounting. The document states: "Overall, our review found that school board financial statements were prepared in accordance with Canadian PSAS."

The tax-rate by-law is enacted only after (and to implement) the municipal budget levy requirement adopted by Council. The 2026 by-law states the Municipal Budget Levy Requirement of $24,457,260 that the rates are calculated to raise. The document states: "AND WHEREAS the Municipal Budget Levy Requirement for Loyalist Township amounts to $24,457,260;"

The by-law applies the established tax rates to the assessed value of all rateable real property according to the latest revised assessment roll (prepared by MPAC). The document states: "AND WHEREAS the assessed value of all rateable real property according to the latest revised assessment roll including for Payment in Lieu properties for Loyalist Township amounts to $2,475,159,600;"

Like all Ontario municipalities, Loyalist Township's audited financial statements are prepared in accordance with Canadian Public Sector Accounting Standards. The document states: "The Ministry of Municipal Affairs and Housing mandates a very detailed financial report which is available on the Ministry's website."

The provincial FIR is populated from each municipality's audited financial statements. Loyalist Township's statements are the source data for its annual FIR submission under Municipal Act s. 294(1). The document states: "Through the FIR template, a standard Excel workbook, the Ministry collects data on municipal financial position and activities ... based on the audited financial statements."
